text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Unity Party, excluded by the renominated Prime Minister Andris Shkele from his coalition, resumed talks with the Democratic Party Saimnieks on forming a political block. Edgars Bans, head of Unity, said it is ready to support the new government.

- Two Socialist party members of parliament said they are ready to support the new Shkele government provided he signs an agreement on the protection of non-citizens' right with the faction. Fatherland & Freedom, the third largest faction, warned his party would withdraw from the coalition if such an agreement was signed.

- President Guntis Ulmanis declined an invitation to the inauguration of the Chechen president on grounds of a busy agenda. Consultations are under way with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to agree on what level Latvia should be represented at the ceremony.
- Latvian Gas company pledges not to lift tariffs as a result of Riga Heat company planning to buy less natural gas.

- Baltic prime ministers agreed during a Tallinn meeting to work out draft agreements on easing transit procedures and on the customs union between Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. The first agreement is to be finalised in five months time, the second early 1998.
- Latvia's internal debt on February 5 was 208 million lats, an increase of more than 11.3 million lats compared to the same period a year ago. The budget deficit amounted to 2.6 million lats.
- The European Union has granted 161,000 ECU to Latvia's Citizenship and Immigration Board to speed up the issuing of non-citizen passports.
- The insurance market recorded a 40.7 million lats rise last year, measured by premium revenues, an increase of 27 percent.
